_what: The board state a human acknowledged, as an axis -> status MAP. This record is not a count: the axis count, the measured count and the gap are read off the map by whoever needs them, never typed beside it (a typed count beside the map it describes is a second thing that can be wrong). scripts/board-production-anchor.mjs checks at pull-request time that this map matches the board the commit renders, so a pull request that changes the board acknowledges it here, in the same pull request. The nightly pulse (.github/workflows/eat-overnight.yml) compares the LIVE board against this map and halts when they differ, which catches a board that changed outside a pull request. A missing or unreadable record is a difference, never a pass.
_acknowledged_note: Acknowledging the board as it now stands: every axis on the map carries a measurement. The nightly pulse was red on 123 consecutive runs (2026-10-05T21:38Z to 2026-11-03T02:38Z) because its expectation did not move with the board. First a literal '22 axis / 22 measured' was typed in the workflow, and every run since axis 23 existed read the board's published GROWTH as drift (#3727 replaced that literal with this map comparison on 2026-11-02). Then this record was the comparison, and #3724 (the ten remaining subject axes measured, and watchdog-ingest added as the 34th) and #3753 (the board re-measured and published) left it behind, so the pulse kept halting and naming the axes that moved (#3848 corrected the map on 2026-11-03). This record is the acknowledgement those 123 runs were asking for, and the pull-request check now asks for it where it can still be cheap.

The counts inside the quoted commit subject are that subject's own words, quoted as a citation; the counts beside this map are read off the map, never typed.
